text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Sudden spike in 5xx and DNS SERVFAILs for inference-eu.redwood.ai (eu-west-1). Triggered PAGER P-12011 at 08:17 UTC. 5xx rate jumped from ~0.15% -> 5.9%. Correlation: increased DNS SERVFAIL/FORMERR from some public resolvers. Please triage.

rachel-sre: Acked P-12011. I'm primary. Checking backend health now. @mark-dns can you run authoritative vs public resolver diffs? Suspect delegation/DS issue given recent zone migration.

mark-dns: Running diffs. Quick outputs:
```
# authoritative NS (ns1.rwdfd.io)
$ dig +dnssec +short A inference-eu.redwood.ai @ns1.rwdfd.io
34.210.11.9

# Cloudflare public resolver
$ dig +dnssec +short A inference-eu.redwood.ai @1.1.1.1
SERVFAIL

# Google public resolver
$ dig +dnssec +short A inference-eu.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8
SERVFAIL

# dig +trace
$ dig +trace inference-eu.redwood.ai
; <<>> DiG 9.10.6 <<>> +trace inference-eu.redwood.ai
...
;; Received 1 answers, 1 authority, 0 additional
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL
```
Authoritative servers return the A record locally, but recursive resolvers with DNSSEC validation enabled are returning SERVFAIL. My hypothesis: DS record for the delegated subdomain was either added/removed incorrectly at the registrar during the migration, so recursive validators consider the chain broken.

luca-netops: Confirmed we rolled the delegation for inference-eu.* to Route53 yesterday and there was an automated DS update attempted by the registrar. We may have an inconsistent DS (wrong digest) currently published at the parent. That would explain validators failing while non-validating resolvers may still work.

rachel-sre: Impact estimate: approx 8-10% of EU traffic uses validating resolvers (based on telemetry) and is failing with SERVFAIL, causing client retries/timeouts and 5xx surface. CS already seeing tickets. Immediate plan?

mark-dns: Immediate mitigation options:
1) If registrar supports it, remove DS record at parent zone to stop validation. This makes the delegation unsecured but restores resolution.
2) If DS is correct on our end, ensure the DS at parent matches our DNSKEY digest and re-trigger DS push.
3) Add short-lived inference-eu-fallback.redwood.ai CNAME to anycast frontdoor and update SDK/edge fallback to prefer it.

rachel-sre: Execute 1 and 3 in parallel: remove DS to restore resolution quickly, and deploy fallback so clients avoid name-based failures. We'll later re-add DS after DNSKEY/DS verification.

luca-netops: Opening registrar ticket now and performing DS removal via registrar API. Command (internal):
```
curl -X POST "https://registrar.api/zone/parent.example/keys/remove" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REG_API" \
  -d '{"delegation":"inference-eu.redwood.ai"}'
```
Ticket REG-2045 opened; taking action at 08:25 UTC.

rachel-sre: Pushing edge fallback and SDK hint. Edge config snippet:
```
hosts:
  - inference-eu.redwood.ai
fallback_hosts:
  - inference-eu-fallback.redwood.ai
  - anycast-inference.redwood.ai
```
Rolling to 4/4 edge clusters.

mark-dns: Added inference-eu-fallback CNAME -> anycast-inference.redwood.ai in Route53 and set TTL=30s. Route53 change id: C-XYZ. Also publishing DNSKEY locally and preparing DS digest if we re-enable DNSSEC.

oncall-bot: Handoff: @rachel-sre primary, @luca-netops secondary. Estimated time to partial mitigation 5-15m. :white_check_mark:

luca-netops: Registrar responded: DS removed at parent at 08:27:12 UTC. Probing now:
```
$ dig +dnssec +short A inference-eu.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8
34.210.11.9
```
Google and Cloudflare resolvers now return the authoritative IP. 5xx rate dropped from 5.9% -> 0.9% over next 4 minutes.

cloudflare-status-bot: Cloudflare: No platform-wide DNS issues. If your domain was recently migrated and DNSSEC was changed, Cloudflare recommends checking DS records at registrar.

dispatch-note: Customer-facing update draft from @sam-cs (08:30 UTC): "We experienced DNS validation errors causing intermittent failures for EU customers. Engineers have implemented temporary fallbacks and removed a DNSSEC delegation while we verify key material. Most traffic is restored; no action required. We'll provide a full incident report after root cause analysis." ETA next update 30m.

rachel-sre: Good recovery. Next steps: verify DNSKEY/DS consistency, coordinate with registrar to re-add DS with correct digest, and create an automated preflight check before future delegation changes. Also add runbook step: 'If delegation migration -> validate DS digest across parent & child before switching live'.

mark-dns: Saving dig traces to /srv/incident/2300009999/traces. Will prepare RCA notes: timeline of registrar DS update, audit logs for the automated DS push, and a proposal to gate DS changes behind a manual review.

sam-cs: Sent customer update at 08:34 UTC and posted incident INC-20260315-04 on status.redwood.ai. Included advice: no action required; SDK fallback rolled out automatically.

rachel-sre: Monitoring for 1 hour. Keeping TTL low (30s) and leaving fallback active for 2 hours. If traffic stable and no recurrence, we'll resolve and write a postmortem focused on DNSSEC migration automation and registrar validation failures.

google-dns-bot: Auto-ticket created: G-DNS-5523 acknowledged receipt of report; they recommend revalidating DS/DS algorithm compatibility. Please provide dig +dnssec traces.

rachel-sre: Thanks everyone. Closing urgent channel in 60 minutes if metrics remain stable. Action items: registrar DS policy, preflight tooling, and automated resolver divergence alerting. Good work. :mechanical_arm:
